court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Akola (FCA No.4 of 2023 and FCA No.11 of 2023)
case_name: Sau. Pooja W/O. Shrikant Kale vs Shrikant Rameshwarrao Kale
facts_of_case: The couple got married in 2017 but started living separately after three months. The wife filed for restitution of conjugal rights while the husband sought annulment or divorce on grounds of cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: A material fact, if disclosed, would have resulted in the husband not agreeing or consenting to the marriage.
legal_principles.held: Though the said disease may not seriously interfere with the married life of the husband, but it is of such a nature, certainly if disclosed, would have resulted in the husband not agreeing or consenting to the marriage

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging concealment to prove that the other party was not informed about a material fact.
legal_principles.held: Though the said disease may not seriously interfere with the married life of the husband, but it is of such a nature, certainly if disclosed, would have resulted in the husband not agreeing or consenting to the marriage

outcome.final_order: The impugned common judgment and decree passed by the Family Court, Akola was set aside.
